title: Ant Jaws Were Used as Stitches for Wounds

scenes.text: Doctors used live ants as stitches.
Pinch a wound shut, hold a driver ant to the skin, and it bites down hard.
Then you twist off its body. The head stays clamped on, with the jaws holding the cut closed.
Ancient Indian texts describe it, and barbers in Greece were still doing it in 1896.
Surgeons stopped when gut thread became easy to get.
Please don't try this at home.

description:
Historical accounts describe ant heads being used to hold wounds closed. The jaws clamp shut on the skin even after the body is removed.
The practice is recorded in ancient India and was still reported in Greece in 1896.
Would you have trusted this?
first_comment: What is the strangest old medical trick you know?
